subject: Clarify metering math & packaging options for BrightCart pilot
messages:
From: Jake Thompson <jake@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Metering math question + packaging / pilot

Marcus —

Quick one from our billing team: we ran a sample of API traces (attached BrightCart_usage_sample.csv) and noticed that some very short user interactions are being rounded up in a way that makes our unit math not line up with the forecast we shared earlier. Two asks:

1) Can you explain (in plain language) how you currently round per-request token usage when requests/responses are small (eg <200 tokens total)? We saw several lines that jump from ~120 tokens to 200 on the invoice.

2) If we commit to a 6-month pilot (targeting ~3M tokens/month), what packaging/discounting options are available? Would we get a different treatment for microcalls during the pilot?

We'd like to close the pilot terms this week if possible — our finance lead is copied.

Thanks,
Jake
BrightCart — Head of Platform

Attachment: BrightCart_usage_sample.csv (csv, 18KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jake Thompson <jake@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Metering math question + packaging / pilot

Jake — thanks for the sample, that helped. Short answer up front: we bill tokens in fixed quanta and apply a per-call aggregation rule for streaming sessions; both interact with the minimums that are applied to short chat-like calls. Below is a clear example plus a proposed pilot concession.

Example (how the rounding is happening today):
- Billing quantum: 50-token units for per-call accounting.
- Aggregation rule: within a single API call we sum request+response tokens, then round UP to the nearest 50.
- Minimum per-call floor: a 150-token floor applies for non-committed customers on streaming endpoints.

So your raw trace: request 80 + response 40 = 120 tokens -> rounded up to 150 because of the 150 minimum. A different trace: 220 tokens -> rounded up to 250 because of 50-unit quantum (no additional minimum).

Impact: small interactions (below the 150 floor) generate a disproportionate uplift relative to raw tokens — that explains the jump you saw from ~120 to 200 on the exported lines.

Pilot packaging proposal (draft):
- 6-month pilot, target 3M tokens/month.
- Pilot price: list price minus 12% discount.
- Metering concession: during pilot we will:
  * waive the 150-token per-call floor for your account (so we only apply the 50-token quantum rounding), and
  * apply a reporting correction on first invoice if the rounding delta exceeds 7% of raw tokens for that month (we credit the overage back as a line-item).

Next steps: Kimberly / Vanessa — can you confirm the concession is feasible from a pricing and risk perspective? If yes I'll send BrightCart a short term sheet and DocuSign.

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: sample lines I pulled (not attaching here)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Metering math question + packaging / pilot

Marcus / Vanessa —

Thanks for flagging — approved with stipulations. A few clarifications and a tighter way to word the concession so CS/Finance have clear guardrails: 

1) Confirmed billing controls: quantum = 50 tokens; per-call totals are summed then rounded up to next quantum. The universal per-call floor (150 tokens) can be waived for BrightCart for the duration of the pilot only.

2) Credit guardrail: the reporting correction should trigger only when (rounded_billed_tokens - raw_tokens) / raw_tokens >= 0.07 AND total raw_tokens in the month >= 500k. This prevents tiny-month churn accounting.

3) Discounting: 12% pilot discount is fine. For a formal committed contract (post-pilot), we can tier discounts to 18% at 6M+ committed monthly tokens.

4) Legal/Procurement ask: pilot must include a one-page addendum limiting the concession to the pilot period and requiring 30 days notice before reverting to default billing. I drafted a short term sheet and attached it: pilot_term_sheet.pdf.

5) Operational note: Vanessa, please ensure the billing pipeline tags BrightCart traffic with account_id=brightcart so the waived-floor logic is applied server-side (and not via manual invoice adjustments).

If all good I recommend Marcus send the one-pager + HubSpot deal update and route the DocuSign link.

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Attachment: pilot_term_sheet.pdf (pdf, 4 pages)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jake Thompson <jake@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, BrightCart Billing <billing@brightcart.com>
Date: 2028-05-18T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Metering math question + packaging / pilot — confirmed next steps

Jake / BrightCart team —

Thanks — summary & next steps below so we're all aligned: 

Summary of agreed pilot terms:
- Pilot length: 6 months (start on signing).
- Target run-rate: ~3M tokens/month.
- Pilot discount: 12% off list.
- Metering concessions:
  * Waive the 150-token per-call floor for pilot traffic (we will still round to 50-token quanta).
  * If monthly rounding delta > 7% AND raw_tokens >= 500k, Redwood will issue a pro-rated credit for the difference on that invoice.
- Post-pilot: default pricing/rules resume unless we sign a committed contract; committing 6M+/mo can move to 18% discount per Kimberly's note.

Action items:
1) Marcus: send the one-page pilot addendum (attached) via DocuSign — link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/EXAMPLE-DS-4821 (sent).
2) BrightCart: review and sign; share preferred start date.
3) Vanessa: confirm billing pipeline tagging (account_id=brightcart) and confirm by 2028-05-20.
4) Kimberly: I'll update HubSpot (deal DEAL-4821) to reflect pilot terms.

Jake — appreciate the quick loop. If you'd like a short call to walk through the microcall math I can schedule 20 minutes tomorrow.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot_term_sheet.pdf (pdf), BrightCart_usage_sample.csv (csv)
